name: issue_867_comfort_family_reactive_mild_day_floor_breach
description: Same defect population as issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_floor_breach.json (day_type whose real classifier.py-derived hvac_mode is "off"), but DAY_TYPE_MILD instead of DAY_TYPE_WARM -- proves the Issue #867 fix covers both day types that share this classification.hvac_mode="off" characteristic, not just the one the live incident happened to be classified as.
notes: Issue #867 root cause: comfort_family_temperature_check()'s guard used to check
`classification.hvac_mode not in ("heat", "cool")` and return early whenever it was "off" --
which classifier.py sets for BOTH DAY_TYPE_WARM and DAY_TYPE_MILD. The existing #858 scenario
(now corrected to hvac_mode="off") only exercises DAY_TYPE_WARM; this scenario exercises
DAY_TYPE_MILD so both members of the affected population are proven, not just one.
A companion ceiling-breach scenario for the "off" population was considered and dropped:
warm/mild days are cooling-native (base_family="cooling", since _apply_comfort_band()'s
active edge falls back to "ceiling" whenever hvac_mode != "heat") -- a ceiling breach on
such a day is never a family SWITCH (there is nothing to escalate to; the FSM is already
sitting in "cooling"), so decide_comfort_family() correctly returns a non-transition outcome
(confirmed via a debug-trace run: `outcome=hold` with `cool_candidate_since` correctly
sustain-confirmed at 120s -- the FSM works exactly as intended, there is just no target family
left to switch to). The only direction that is ever a genuine family switch for the
hvac_mode="off" population is the floor breach into heating -- which this scenario and its
warm-day sibling both cover. The symmetric heating-native population (DAY_TYPE_COOL/COLD)
always derives hvac_mode="heat" from real classifier.py, never "off", so no equivalent
"off"-population ceiling-breach case exists to test.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md #10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness (revert-test): reintroducing the old
`classification.hvac_mode not in ("heat", "cool")` guard makes this scenario fail --
comfort_family_temperature_check() would return early on every tick (hvac_mode="off"),
and comfort_family_switch_by would never fire since no second classification event runs.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's #858/#867 note documents
that the reactive check's applicability is band-based, covering both warm and mild.
(c) Occupant experience: a home drifting below the comfort floor on a mild day (native
hvac_mode=off, same population as the live incident) now gets heat engaged within about a
minute and a half of the drift being detected, instead of the up-to-30-minute wait that
silently returned after Issue #858 first shipped.

events.note: Mild-day classification. hvac_mode=off matches what classifier.py actually derives for DAY_TYPE_MILD -- _apply_comfort_band() still arms a real floor/ceiling-active comfort band regardless. Only classification event in this scenario -- everything after this is driven by temp_update alone.

First breach tick: 1F below comfort_heat(66). Cold-start engine -- nothing recorded as recently cooling, so the recency-gated deadband is already 0F. comfort_family_temperature_check() fires reactively (indoor < band.floor), re-enters apply_classification() -- sustain-confirm candidate starts here, not yet confirmed (elapsed 0s < 90s).
120s after the first breach tick (>90s sustain window). Reactive check fires again, sustain-confirms, escalates to heating -- with no second classification event ever having run.

assertions.reason: Baseline: mild day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally, even though the day's native recommendation is hvac_mode=off.

Issue #867: the switch to heating lands by 06:17, driven entirely by the reactive temperature-tick path, on a day type whose classification.hvac_mode is "off" -- proving the guard fix covers DAY_TYPE_MILD as well as DAY_TYPE_WARM.
Final engine state confirms the family actually escalated, not just an emitted event.
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A floor breach on a mild (hvac_mode=off) day resolves to heat within one sustain-confirm window of the reactive temperature tick (Issue #867).
verdict.observed_behavior: Single classification event at 06:00 (mild/off), indoor falls below the floor via temp_update alone at 06:15 and 06:17 -- comfort family escalates to heating by 06:17, driven entirely by the reactive tick.
verdict.expected_behavior: The reactive comfort-family check's applicability must be decided by whether a comfort band is armed, not by the classifier's native hvac_mode recommendation -- mild days get the same fast-detection guarantee as warm days for the one direction (floor breach) that is ever a genuine family switch for this population.
